messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert - GeoDNS: elevated DNS failures for EU regions (api.redwood.ai). Multiple customer reports of 502s/latency from eu-west. Auto-paging oncall.

mike (oncall): ack, looking. seeing 502s in the error dashboard, will pull DNS traces.

carla: I can reproduce timeouts - dig +trace against Cloudflare authoritative shows intermittent SERVFAILs for api.redwood.ai in eu resolvers. Route53 entries are in the mix due to our GeoDNS failover. Likely propagation / resolver inconsistency.

mike (oncall): timeline? when did this start? any config changes?

carla: started ~1894501000 (about 5m before page). No infra deploys from us. Cloudflare did a certificate rekey earlier but that's unrelated afaict.

sre-jen: joining handoff. tagging @paul (networking) — can you validate Cloudflare health and Route53 config?

paul (networking): on it. quick check: Cloudflare authoritative responses from EU PoPs are returning SERVFAIL 20-30% of the time, while US PoPs are fine. Route53 latency-based records appear to still point some clients to eu nodes (ttl was 300). Combined, some resolvers get Cloudflare failure -> cached Route53 answer -> hit degraded eu backend.

mike (oncall): impact estimate? which customers/regions?

support-elaine: reports from three enterprise customers in EU - intermittent 502s for API calls, user-visible timeouts. Ticket #INC-4821 opened, CS notified.

ops-bot: status-page: creating incident 'EU DNS instability causing API errors' (link: https://status.redwood.example/incident/INC-4821)

carla: mitigation plan (quick):
1) shift GeoDNS weight away from eu-west to us-east to drain traffic (Route53 change).
2) lower TTL to 60 on affected records so changes propagate quickly.
3) temporarily disable Cloudflare proxy (orange -> gray) for api.* to bypass any layer of Cloudflare's network and serve authoritative A records directly.
4) add explicit fallback A records pointing to US pool IPs while we investigate.
5) open ticket with Cloudflare and provide packet captures.

mike (oncall): execute 1-4. I'll coordinate Route53 change.

carla: I'll toggle Cloudflare proxied state and lower TTL.

paul (networking): prepping change batch for Route53. using hosted zone Z3EXAMPLE. change file:
```json
{
  "Comment": "geo weight shift - eu->us temporary",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "api.redwood.ai.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "us-primary",
        "Weight": 100,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "52.10.20.30"}],
        "TTL": 60
      }
    },
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "api.redwood.ai.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "eu-backup",
        "Weight": 0,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "3.120.45.60"}],
        "TTL": 60
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

paul (networking): command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE --change-batch file://geo-weight-swap.json`

mike (oncall): running now.

(paused ~30s)

mike (oncall): Route53 change submitted - change id C12345, propagation starting.

carla: toggled Cloudflare proxy to DNS-only for api.redwood.ai on the zonal dashboard. Lowered TTL to 60.

support-elaine: customer updates sent: "We're aware of DNS instability affecting EU traffic, working on mitigation; temporary reroute applied."

ops-bot: metric watch: DNS error-rate (CF authoritative) peaked at 28% -> now at 5% after changes. API 5xx rate in EU decreased from 6% -> 1.2%.

paul (networking): added explicit A records for failover to US pool; health checks configured to fail back when eu nodes healthy.

sre-jen: status update for execs: initial mitigation applied, traffic shifted to US, customer impact reduced, monitoring closely. Severity moving from P1 -> P2.

status-bot: status page updated: "Partial outage in EU region affecting API traffic due to DNS provider instability. Mitigations in place. Investigating root cause with Cloudflare and AWS Route53."

carla: opened ticket with Cloudflare support (ticket CF-987654) with dig traces and pcap. Cloudflare acknowledged and started investigation into EU PoP anomalies.

mike (oncall): keeping watch for 30m. If no regressions, we'll leave geo weight shifted and keep TTL low for 1h, then gradually move traffic back. Postmortem assigned to networking (paul, carla).

support-elaine: customers asking for RCA ETA. can we commit to a timeframe?

sre-jen: we'll have an RCA initial summary within 24h and a full postmortem in 72h. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: alert cleared in monitoring pulse, but watch remains.

paul (networking): Cloudflare follow-up: they saw a config rollout in EU edge that caused a subset of authoritative responses to be malformed; rollback in progress on their side. They will share internal timeline.

mike (oncall): noted. planning to restore original geo weights gradually after 1 hour of stable metrics.

(about 45m later)

mike (oncall): metrics stable for 40m. starting canary to move 20% traffic back to EU (update Route53 weights).

paul (networking): canary applied. monitoring.

(10m)

ops-bot: EU 5xx rate steady at baseline, DNS errors down to ~0.5%.

sre-jen: lowering incident severity to P3; customers notified of resolution steps. Postmortem skeleton created: https://wiki.redwood.example/INC-4821-postmortem.

carla: action items captured:
- formalize playbook for Cloudflare authoritative fallbacks
- automate TTL/weight swap runbook
- add synthetic DNS checks from multiple regions to catch resolver inconsistencies

mike (oncall): thanks team. handing back to regular oncall.

sre-jen: closing slack thread for incident. postmortem owners: paul (networking), carla. CC: support-elaine, engineering-paul.

support-elaine: thanks all, will follow up with affected customers with RCA when available.

incident-bot: incident INC-4821 resolved (status: monitoring).
